clue.text: Expert sticking to specific plants and animals

indicators.note: one thing sticking to another sits right against it, so the two pieces are joined end to end

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast who knows a subject well
a particular genus of succulent plants

explanation.surface: A specialist devoted to certain flora and fauna, a naturalist with a narrow field.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo are large wild oxen, so the plural names a group of big creatures of the plains.

clue.text: One footing it, perhaps, in an attempt to take exercise

indicators.note: the attempt is made to take something in, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: a bid is a try at something
physical education, the school subject

explanation.surface: Someone walking somewhere as a way of getting some exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: anything on two feet can be footing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-legged creature walks on its feet, so a walker is an example of such an animal.

clue.text: Position in rugby for TSE?

blocks.note: first meaning: a back-line player who links the scrum half with the three-quarters
second meaning, read literally: TSE is one half of TSETSE, the African biting insect

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where the poet T S Eliot would play if picked for a rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: TSE looks like Eliot's initials, but it is half the name of the tsetse, a fly of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby union number ten plays this role, and the insect's name split down the middle literally gives half a fly.

clue.text: Grey does give a toss

blocks.note: taken as written
a shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Someone grey-faced and indifferent, who does not give a toss about anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does give a toss' reads as the slang for caring; in fact 'a toss' is simply a throw. A coconut shy is a fairground stall where balls are thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is pale grey powder left after burning, so something coloured like it is pallid grey.

clue.text: Billy's eclipsing top seed

definitions.note: the clue's singular stands for a grain crop named in the plural

indicators.note: eclipsing hides from view, so the top letter of the word is blotted out

blocks.note: a billy is a male goat, and the possessive 's gives the final S

explanation.surface: A billy goat's prize animal, the top seed in some farmyard tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the top is the first letter, so G goes. 'Top seed' sounds like a tennis ranking, but 'top' belongs to the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: The cereal crop is grown and harvested for its grain, which is sown as seed and eaten as porridge.

clue.text: From outset, wait uncomfortably for the result

definitions.text: From outset, wait uncomfortably for the result

indicators.note: something uncomfortable is out of its proper position, so the letters are reset

blocks.note: the ten letters of the two words together

explanation.surface: From the very start, someone waits anxiously for an outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the wordplay is the shuffled words, and the full sentence describes the anxious waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure an anxious period until it ends is the idiom, as a nervous candidate does awaiting exam marks.

clue.text: Basin or sink?

blocks.note: first meaning: a variant spelling of stoup, a basin for holy water in a church
second meaning: to lower oneself, morally or physically

explanation.walkthrough: Basin and sink look like two kitchen fittings, but the second is a verb meaning to descend to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A church font for holy water takes this spelling as a variant, and bending down or demeaning oneself is the verb sense.

clue.text: Farms in US maybe succeeded following cut after cut

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the abbreviation is put at the end

blocks.note: a cut is a share, as in a cut of the profits
to crop is to cut short
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: American farms where the land was handed on, one harvest following another.
explanation.walkthrough: Sharecropping is an American system in which a tenant farms land and pays the owner part of the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant who works land for a landlord in return for a portion of the crop is said to farm it this way.

clue.text: View of one of those known to be fully knowledgeable holding good

indicators.note: holding means clasping something inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.clueFragment: one of those known to be fully knowledgeable
blocks.note: someone who is expert 'knows their onions'
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: The considered view of an expert who knows everything there is to know.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'know your onions' is British slang for being expert, so the long phrase points to the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a belief or judgement someone holds about a matter, which is exactly a personal stance.

clue.text: Tap round rib area, including heart finally in this investigation

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end
finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept
including means taking something in, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the chest is the part of the body enclosed by the ribs
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A doctor tapping round the ribs, listening to the heart during an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' is not the middle letters here: 'finally' takes its last letter. The surface looks like a chest examination, but the answer tests skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor tapes a small amount of allergen to the skin to investigate whether a reaction develops.

clue.text: Medical professional has the assailant on film

blocks.note: Hitchcock's 1960 thriller
taken as written
a violent sexual attacker

explanation.surface: A clinician whose attacker has been caught on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the film first in the answer, with the other two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist who treats mental and emotional disorders by talking is a professional working in the field of health.

clue.text: Cart in enclosed space turned round

indicators.note: turned round means facing the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: a yard is an area surrounded by walls or buildings

explanation.surface: A cart being turned round in a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A low flat wagon without sides, traditionally used by brewers to deliver barrels, is a kind of horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Soak is husband? That's rather exaggerated!

blocks.note: to steep is to soak in liquid
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that calling the husband a drunk is going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' tempts as a noun meaning a drunkard, but it is the verb. Steep also means excessive, as in a steep price.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep demand is excessive or unreasonable, and the -ish suffix makes it 'somewhat', so a bit over the top.

clue.text: Form to mark with an "X" for seats for independent parliamentarians

blocks.note: to cross is to mark with a cross
a form is a long backless bench, as in a school

explanation.surface: A ballot form on which a voter marks an X for a candidate's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like paperwork, but it is an old word for a bench. In the House of Lords, members belonging to no party sit on the benches running across the chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British House of Lords the non-party members sit on benches set crosswise to the government and opposition sides.

clue.text: Fellow at top university's concerned with plants

blocks.note: Herb, a man's name, is just some fellow
ace means first-rate
OU is the Open University, a British distance-learning institution, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A don who has reached the top of his university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' and 'university' suggest a college fellow, but the fellow is just a man called Herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes soft-stemmed plants, as in a border full of perennial flowers, so it relates to vegetation.

clue.text: Stay and calm down?

blocks.note: first meaning: a postponement, as in a stay of execution
second meaning, cryptically: removing the 'ferment', or agitation, from something

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay where you are and keep calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: 'de-' undoes, and ferment is unrest, so taking away the unrest calms things.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting off a court sentence or military service is a postponement, and the split word whimsically suggests removing turmoil.

clue.text: Resolution to face duke (fist), or turn away?

indicators.note: a resolution breaks something down into its parts, which can then be put together anew

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between squaring up to a fighter's fist or backing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' is also slang for a fist, which makes the bracket look like a gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: To disaffect someone is to alienate them, making their loyalty turn away from a leader or cause.

clue.text: Taking unfamiliar way, gets lost in the mountains

indicators.note: whatever gets lost is no longer there, so that part drops out of the word

blocks.note: strange means not known before
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A walker who takes an unfamiliar path and gets lost in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed street abbreviation happens to sit at the front, leaving the last five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of peaks such as the Rockies forms a line of high ground, which is the collective noun for them.

clue.text: Having killed son with violence, swings

blocks.note: past tense of slay
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A murderer who has killed his son violently, as in a grim tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With violence' looks like how the killing happened, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To slew is to turn or slide round suddenly and uncontrollably, as a skidding car does.

clue.text: Take nothing away from German prince with a complex daughter

indicators.note: nothing is the round letter for zero, and taking it away removes that letter

blocks.note: an Elector was a German prince entitled to elect the Holy Roman Emperor
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice not to deprive a German prince of anything, nor his troubled daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take nothing away' reads as 'leave intact', but nothing is O and it is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was Agamemnon's daughter, and her name labels the Freudian complex of a girl's attachment to her father.

clue.text: Pornographic material in this draft

blocks.note: a blue film is a pornographic one
print is printed cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Someone finding pornography in a manuscript draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like reading matter, but it is cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed technical drawing or early plan of work is an outline to be developed, so a preliminary version.

clue.text: For limited period, looking healthy and full of energy

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within

blocks.note: in trim means in good physical shape
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone looking fit and lively, but only for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is a stopgap that lasts only until something permanent replaces it, so it is temporary.

clue.text: Enid's response?

blocks.note: surface reading: a reply from someone called Enid, perhaps the children's author Enid Blyton
setter's reading: the name read from its end is DINE, a word meaning to eat or to give food to

explanation.walkthrough: A woman's name looks like a person; read backwards it spells a verb for eating, which the answer describes as reversed nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction or comments given in return about a performance count as a reply, and the split phrase describes Enid turned round.

clue.text: Cut by sharp weapon, or shot?

blocks.note: first meaning: a wound made with a knife
second meaning: an attempt, as in 'have a go'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' tempts as a gunshot wound next to the knife wound, but it means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife thrust makes a wound, and having a go at something is an informal word for a try.

clue.text: 1 across performing after "Encore"

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other, so the second word comes last

blocks.note: bis is a call for a repeat performance
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: Buffaloes performing again after the audience cries for more.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to the plural animals at 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The American plains animals called buffalo are properly a kind of wild ox, and the word serves as singular or plural.

clue.text: Our mother, by Jove!

blocks.note: surface reading: an exclamation of surprise about someone's mother
setter's reading: a mother whose children were fathered by Jupiter, so the speakers are the twins Castor and Pollux

explanation.walkthrough: 'By Jove!' looks like an old oath; read literally, it names the father. Zeus, the Roman Jove, came to her as a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she bore Helen and the twins Castor and Pollux to the king of the gods.

clue.text: Very pretty is Peg when carrying little weight

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A girl named Peg looks very pretty when she is slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a girl's name; here it is the golfing tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something twee is excessively dainty, quaint or sweet, pretty to the point of sentimentality.

clue.text: Admitting error on taking in what one has said

definitions.text: taking in what one has said

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for retracting a statement in humiliation

blocks.clueFragment: taking in what one has said
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: consuming one's own remarks

explanation.surface: Someone backtracking on being misquoted by taking in what they said.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the idiom literally, with taking in as swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to retract a claim, usually humbly, after being shown to have been mistaken.

clue.text: With temperature and skin disorder, takes to bunk

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
a rash is an outbreak of red spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A patient with a fever and a rash takes to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed for the sick patient, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk is short for bunkum, empty talk, and rubbish is another word for nonsense of that kind.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer admitting setback for senior politicians

indicators.note: a word set back is put the other way round, here the word set itself
admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the pollen-bearing part of a flower
taken as written, from inside the indicator

explanation.surface: Part of a gaffe acknowledging a setback for the party's elder statesmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a blunder, but it is a flower. The word setback contains both the letters and the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced and respected political leaders are called by this term, especially those who rise above party.
